title: sus-grad-correlation: suspiciousness and gradient correlation experiments for neural networks
description:
Code and reproduction container for two experiments asking whether the neurons that spectrum-based fault localisation (SBFL) calls suspicious are the same neurons that carry a large loss gradient.

Experiment 1 trains 100 randomly initialised copies of each of four model/dataset pairs (MLP and LeNet-5, on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST) and correlates suspiciousness against the per-neuron gradient across that population, at epochs 0, 1 and 10.

Experiment 2 trains one seeded copy of each pair for 200 epochs, measuring after every epoch, and follows both a single neuron and the whole-model population across the run.

Both experiments reproduce from a clean checkout through Docker or through Python; see the README for the exact command sequences.

Supplement to: An Empirical Analysis of the Correlation between Suspiciousness Scores and Loss Gradients in Neural Networks.
